title_prefix: The outbound full-relay refill dials a s
mechanism: replace-disconnected-peers (src/node/peers.lisp:744-848) refills the outbound full-relay slots with a plain DOLIST over (node-known-addresses node) in list order (src/node/peers.lisp:805). The only writer of that slot in the whole tree is src/node/peers.lisp:541, inside connect-to-peers (grep over src/ and tests/: the other hits are the accessor definition at src/node/state.lisp:51, two comments, and one test at tests/networking/eclipse-dos-tests.lisp:2336). sb-introspect:who-calls reports exactly two callers of connect-to-peers -- %sync-thread-connect (start-up, src/node/init.lisp:946) and %sync-offline-activation (src/node/init.lisp:1180) -- and the sync loop reaches the second only when (>= (length (node-peers *node*)) 1) is false (src/node/init.lisp:1218-1220). So the refill pool is a boot-time snapshot of at most (* max-peers 8) select-dialable-address picks plus DNS seeds, the fixed-seed fallback and anchors, and it is rebuilt only if the node reaches ZERO peers of any kind (a surviving block-relay or inbound peer keeps the count above zero). Inside the walk there is no last-attempt cooldown, no GetChance weighting, no IsTerrible filter and no addrman Select at all; the only skips are 'already connected to this address' and 'this /16 already holds an outbound peer'. Also note that `connected' only increments on a SUCCESSFUL handshake, so failed dials do not end the pass: one sweep walks the whole candidate list rather than `needed' entries. Core's ThreadOpenConnections re-samples addrman on every attempt (refs/bitcoin/src/net.cpp:2804-2822), gives up after 100 tries per pass (:2789-2791), and skips any candidate whose last try is under 10 minutes old until 30 candidates have been rejected ('if (current_time - addr_last_try < 10min && nTries < 30) continue;', :2839-2841), on top of addrman's own GetChance (0.01x within 10 minutes of the last attempt, 0.66^nAttempts) and IsTerrible. The frozen pool is specific to this path: maintain-block-relay-peers (src/node/peers.lisp:1069-1089) and maybe-do-feeler (:1116-1149) both draw from addrman through %addrman-pick-unconnected.
consequence: Two, and both are the finding's. (1) No back-off: maintain-peers runs once per sync pass (src/node/init.lisp:1117), whose idle window is bounded at 30 seconds, so an address that keeps refusing us is re-dialled roughly every 30 seconds forever, in the same fixed order, where Core would not touch it again for 10 minutes and would then pick it with probability 0.01 x 0.66^nAttempts. That is wasted dial bandwidth and it is the mechanism behind the same addresses recurring in the live logs. (2) The eight outbound full-relay slots -- the ones that carry eclipse resistance -- can only ever be filled from the boot snapshot. Every address learned from addr gossip after start-up lands in addrman and never in this list, so a node whose boot candidates go stale keeps dialling a dead set indefinitely while addrman holds thousands of live entries, and because the block-relay slots and inbound peers keep the peer count above zero, the zero-peer branch that would rebuild the pool is never taken. Held at S2 rather than S1: the node still follows the chain on its block-relay peers, feelers and block-relay refill still reach addrman, and a genuine zero-peer state does rebuild the pool.
evidence: Worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-p2p-s2, warm image bitcoin-lisp-sbcl:2.6.5-4, probe file ga11-probe/p2p.lisp (scratch, not committed). (a) Reproduced independently: %dial-outbound-peer stubbed to record and fail, five replace-disconnected-peers sweeps on a node with four known addresses -> (:DIALS-IN-ORDER ("203.0.113.1" "198.51.100.7" "192.0.2.9" "10.9.0.4" x5) :DISTINCT 4 :TOTAL 20 :ADDRMAN-PICK-CALLS 0 :ADDRMAN-SELECT-CALLS 0 :KNOWN-ADDRESSES-LIST-EQ T). Same order every sweep, four dials per sweep (the whole list, because none succeeded), and both addrman entry points (%addrman-pick-unconnected, bl.net:select-dialable-address) instrumented and never called. (b) Counter-probe with a POPULATED address book (59 records across 40 /16 groups, built with bl.net:address-book-add): three sweeps -> the identical four boot addresses, 12 dials, :ADDRMAN-PICK-CALLS 0 :ADDRMAN-SELECT-CALLS 0. A book entry is never a refill candidate. (c) Counter-probe on refresh paths: sb-introspect:who-calls 'bl::connect-to-peers -> exactly %SYNC-OFFLINE-ACTIVATION (src/node/init.lisp) and %SYNC-THREAD-CONNECT (src/node/init.lisp); grep for known-addresses over src/ and tests/ finds one setf (src/node/peers.lisp:541). Feelers, getaddr/addr ingestion and the periodic peers.dat dump all write addrman, none writes node-known-addresses. (d) Core read at refs/bitcoin/src/net.cpp:2780-2870 for the per-attempt Select, the netgroup test and the 10-minute skip. NOT verified here: the finding's attribution of a specific FRACTION of the 50-70 'connection dead' lines per hour on the live nodes -- no live log is present in this checkout, and that line is emitted by handle-peer-fin (src/networking/ibd.lisp:1591) only for a peer that already completed a handshake and whose socket then died, so the redial loop bounds the RATE (one full walk of the candidate list per <=30 s maintenance tick) and explains the REPETITION of the same address, but the count itself cannot be derived from this worktree.
fix_shape: Make the refill draw per attempt instead of from a boot list. Replace the DOLIST over node-known-addresses with Core's loop shape: up to 100 tries per pass, each try a fresh addrman draw through the same %addrman-pick-unconnected / select-dialable-address call maintain-block-relay-peers already uses, keeping the existing already-connected and /16 netgroup tests, and adding Core's cooldown -- skip a candidate whose last attempt is under 10 minutes old until 30 candidates have been rejected (net.cpp:2839-2841) -- plus the terrible/desirable-services filters addrman already supports. peer-address-last-attempt is already stamped on every dial by %record-dial-attempt (src/node/peers.lisp:276), so the cooldown's input exists. node-known-addresses then seeds only the FIRST fill; anchors, DNS and fixed seeds keep their precedence by being written into addrman rather than into a separate list. Two regression tests are load-bearing: an address dialled and failed must not be re-dialled inside the cooldown window, and an address added to the book AFTER start-up must become a refill candidate -- the second is what the current code cannot do at all.
